oi.text: Operating income and margin . Operating income increased compared to the prior-year period primarily due to higher revenue. Operating margin remained relatively consistent with the prior-year period, as approximately $1.5 million of expenses associated with the annual HUB conference, which occurred in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the fourth quarter of 2025, offset a portion of the benefit from higher revenue.

ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses . Selling, general and administrative expenses consist of salaries and employee benefits, commissions and amortization of deferred commissions, stock-based compensation, employee travel and lodging, third party software subscription and platform costs, marketing costs, facility expenses, office expenses, fees for professional services, provision for credit losses, and other operational expenses. Personnel costs within selling, general and administrative expenses are associated with individuals in sales, marketing, finance, accounting, business development, human resources, administrative, product development, internal information systems, and executive management. Selling, general and administrative expenses were $12.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12.3 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to a $1.1 million reduction in stock-based compensation expense, including the completion of amortization related to previously disclosed executive equity award amendments and the forfeiture of awards associated with the departure of the Company's former Chief Financial Officer. These decreases were partially offset by increased marketing expenditures, higher software subscription costs related to ongoing technology investments, and increased travel expenses.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses . Selling, general and administrative expenses consist of salaries and employee benefits, commissions and amortization of deferred commissions, stock-based compensation, employee travel and lodging, third party software subscription and platform costs, marketing costs, facility expenses, office expenses, fees for professional services, provision for credit losses, and other operational expenses. Personnel costs within selling, general and administrative expenses are associated with individuals in sales, marketing, finance, accounting, business development, human resources, administrative, product development, internal information systems, and executive management. Selling, general and administrative expenses were $12.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12.3 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to a $1.1 million reduction in stock-based compensation expense, including the completion of amortization related to previously disclosed executive equity award amendments and the forfeiture of awards associated with the departure of the Company's former Chief Financial Officer. These decreases were partially offset by increased marketing expenditures, higher software subscription costs related to ongoing technology investments, and increased travel expenses.

da_op.text: Depreciation and amortization . Depreciation and amortization expenses decreased in the 2026 period compared to the 2025 period due to lower amortization expense resulting from a finite-lived intangible asset becoming fully amortized.

tax.text: Provision for income taxes and effective tax rate . Provision for income taxes increased compared to the prior-year period primarily due to an increase in operating income and increase in the rate impacted by non-deductible executive compensation under IRC Section 162(m).

net.text: In addition to consolidated GAAP financial measures, we review various non-GAAP financial measures that management believes to be important in the evaluation of its operating results and performance, including “Adjusted Net Income,” “Adjusted Earnings per Share,” “Adjusted EBITDA,” “Adjusted EBITDA Margin,” “Free Cash Flow,” and “Free Cash Flow Margin.”

ocf.text: Our cash flows from operating activities primarily consist of net income adjusted for non-cash items including depreciation and amortization, deferred income taxes, share-based compensation, and the effect of working capital changes. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, cash provided by operating activities decreased compared to the same period in 2025 primarily due to lower net income net of non-cash items and working capital changes. Working capital changes were mainly driven by trade accounts receivable and prepaid expenses primarily due to timing of billings and payments, and higher deferred revenue, partially offset by the timing of income tax payments and lower accrued expense balances.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization . Depreciation and amortization expenses decreased in the 2026 period compared to the 2025 period due to lower amortization expense resulting from a finite-lived intangible asset becoming fully amortized.

capex.text: We paid cash of $4.2 million for capital expenditures in the nine months ended September 30, 2026. These expenditures consisted primarily of computer hardware and software, and costs related to software development for our Human Understanding® solutions.

intro.text: For more than 45 years, NRC Health (NASDAQ: NRC) has led the charge to humanize healthcare and support organizations in their understanding of each unique individual. NRC Health’s commitment to Human Understanding® helps leading healthcare systems get to know the patients, families, consumers, employees, and communities they serve on a human level. Guided by its uniquely empathic heritage, human-centered approach, unmatched national market research, and emphasis on consumer preferences, NRC Health is transforming the healthcare experience, creating strong outcomes across the healthcare journey. For more information, email info@nrchealth.com, or visit www.nrchealth.com.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our ten largest customers collectively accounted for 20%, 17%, and 15% of our total revenue in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
Direct expenses represented 38% of revenue in 2025 and 40% of revenue in 2024.
Consequently, we rely on a combination of copyright and trade secret laws and associate nondisclosure agreements to protect our systems, survey instruments and procedures.
We depend on contract renewals, including retention of key customers, for a large share of our revenue and our operating results could be adversely affected.
We rely on a limited number of key customers for a substantial portion of our revenue.
Our ability to provide timely and accurate performance measurement and improvement services to our customers depends on our ability to collect large quantities of high-quality data through surveys.
The loss of any of our key vendors could impair our ability to perform our customer services and result in lower revenues and income.

If receptivity to our survey methods by respondents declines, or, for some other reason, their willingness to complete and return surveys declines, or if we, for any reason, cannot rely on the integrity of the data we receive, then our revenue could be adversely affected with a corresponding effect on our operating and net income.
Consequently, we rely on a combination of copyright, trade secret laws, and associate nondisclosure agreements to protect our systems, survey instruments, and procedures.

Any system failure, inability to upgrade or update, or security breach (including cyber-attacks) related to our information technology systems may also impact third parties that we rely on in our business and could result in a hinderance to the services provided by the Company or such third parties, as the case may be, and may have a material adverse effect on our business.
We currently depend on our partner’s technology to perform certain services for our customers.
Our ability to achieve our goals and earnings growth depends on our ability to grow our revenue and achieve the appropriate cost structure for our revenues.
Our success will also depend on our ability to hire, train, and retain skilled personnel in all areas of our business.

The payment and amount of future dividends, if any, is at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend on our future earnings, financial condition, general business conditions, alternative uses of our earnings and cash and other factors.

As of December 31, 2025, our principal sources of liquidity included $4.1 million of cash and cash equivalents, up to $30 million of unused borrowings under our Revolving Loan and an additional $27.6 million on our Delayed Draw Term Loan.
